week.record: data/week-33.json at origin/e0/week-33 e370be9 (PR #8). That record is being corrected for day leads and outlet counts; nothing here depends on either.
week.lead: JD Vance blames the Iran war for the Republican midterm defeat (cluster 2ec1fcb8)
week.mechanism: A war fought abroad comes home as higher prices and a closed sea lane, the governing party loses a national election, and a leader inside that party names the war as the reason.

method.order: Mechanism fit first (0 to 5). Asset availability (0 to 5) only breaks ties between equal fits, and among equal fits media already in a void document ledger wins. no-bridge is applied before scoring.
method.no_bridge: A candidate is excluded when its own story cannot be told without naming an entity from the week's stories (the lead, the day leads, the margins).
method.asset_inputs: void history evidence ledgers at voidnews@cd8a126 (entries, rights: public, recordings); void document ledgers at document@b62c4fa (films/panama-canal) and on the render machine (~/document-work/<film>/*-ledger.json); Wikimedia Commons imageinfo read on 2026-11-12 for the chosen echo only.

candidates.mechanism: A war fought far away comes home as rising prices and a strained dollar, the governing party's own voters turn on it in its first primary, and its leader, naming the war, says he will not run again.
candidates.fit_reason: War abroad, cost at home through prices, a vote inside the governing party, and its own leader naming the war, all in one period document (the 31 March 1968 address). No sea lane closes.
candidates.bridge: clear: the story needs none of the week's named actors (see no_bridge_watch for the home-frame words)

candidates.mechanism: Submarines close the sea lanes, food and fuel prices climb at home, and the governing party loses both houses at a midterm its President had asked voters to make a vote on the war.
candidates.fit_reason: Sea lane, prices and a lost midterm; no held document of a party figure naming the war as the cause.
candidates.bridge: risk: the story names Britain and France, both in the week's record (the 5 Nov day beat is British)

candidates.mechanism: A stalemated war abroad brings price controls and a wage freeze at home, and the governing party loses the presidency after twenty years.
candidates.fit_reason: War and prices fit; no sea lane, and the held ledger has no price or home-front material and no party figure naming the war.

candidates.mechanism: A city's grain route through a strait is cut during a long war abroad, and its assembly votes under the cost.
candidates.fit_reason: Strait and cost at home fit; no election turns out a governing party.

chosen.reason: Highest mechanism fit, tied with world-war-i; the tie goes to assets (3 against 1), and world-war-i also risks bridging through Britain. No candidate with existing document media fits at 4 or more, so the document-media preference does not decide this pick.
chosen.mechanism: A war fought far away comes home as rising prices and a strained dollar, the governing party's own voters turn on it in its first primary, and its leader, naming the war, says he will not run again.
chosen.fit_gap: No sea lane closes in this echo. The Echo shows the cost at home and the leader's own words; it does not reach for a sea parallel (the 1964 Gulf of Tonkin incident lies outside the told story and is not used as a hook).
chosen.as_of_basis: the evening of Sunday 31 March 1968 in Washington, when the President's address was broadcast live (the Daily Diary entry for the date, e33-echo-04). Nothing dated or made public after it enters the Echo.
outside_horizon: the killings at My Lai of 16 March 1968, not public until November 1969
the Pentagon Papers (completed 1969, published 1971), although public domain and in the history ledger
the assassinations of 4 April and 5 June 1968
the passage of the tax surcharge in June 1968
chosen.told_story: Tet (30 January 1968) and its pictures; the cost at home as the President stated it (prices, interest rates, the dollar, the deficit); his own party's first primary; the address of 31 March, on the desk as a draft page and heard in its own sound.

no_bridge_watch.in_the_period_text: The 31 March address names the United Kingdom and the Soviet Union (as the Geneva co-chairmen); those passages are not quoted. The chosen quotes say 'my party', not its name.
no_bridge_watch.needs_a_ruling: Home-frame words that both stories share: United States, America, President, Washington, Congress, Senate, White House, primary. The no-bridge lint as the bible words it would flag them, and every candidate on the plan's shortlist shares them. This pick reads the lint's week-side list as the week's named actors, places and parties, and flags that reading for the lint's author.
